import Mathlib

inductive Color
| Red
| Black
deriving Inhabited, BEq

inductive Node
| Empty : Node
| Tree  (color : Color) (val : Int) (left : Node) (right : Node) : Node
deriving Inhabited

def view (t : Node) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => ∅
  | Node.Tree _ v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_red (t : Node) : Bool :=
  match t with
  | Node.Tree Color.Red _ _ _ => true
  | _ => false

def get_color (t : Node) : Color :=
  match t with
  | Node.Tree c _ _ _ => c
  | Node.Empty => Color.Black -- Empty nodes are black

def is_bst (t : Node) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => True
  | Node.Tree _ v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

-- Black Height: Returns -1 if invalid
def black_height (t : Node) : Int :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => 1
  | Node.Tree c _ l r =>
    let lh := black_height l
    let rh := black_height r
    if lh ≠ -1 ∧ rh ≠ -1 ∧ lh = rh then
      if c == Color.Black then lh + 1 else lh
    else
      -1

def get_left (t : Node) : Option Node :=
  match t with | Node.Tree _ _ l _ => some l | _ => none

def get_right (t : Node) : Option Node :=
  match t with | Node.Tree _ _ _ r => some r | _ => none

def is_not_empty (t : Node) : Prop :=
  match t with | Node.Empty => False | _ => True

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def rotate_right_precond (t : Node) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  match t with
  | Node.Tree _ _ l _ =>
    -- Strictly match Dafny/Verus: Only require Left child to be Red.
    -- The Double-Red context is checked by the caller (insert), not this helper.
    is_red l
  | _ => False
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def rotate_right (t : Node) 
    (h_precond : rotate_right_precond t) : Node :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  match t with
  | Node.Tree c v (Node.Tree _ lv ll lr) r =>
      -- Lift the left (red) child: it becomes the new root and keeps the old
      -- root's color; the old root turns Red and moves to the right.
      Node.Tree c lv ll (Node.Tree Color.Red v lr r)
  | _ => Node.Empty
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def rotate_right_postcond (t : Node) (result : Node)
    (_ : rotate_right_precond t) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  view result = view t ∧
  is_bst t → is_bst result ∧
  match result, t with
  | Node.Tree c' _ _ r', Node.Tree c _ _ _ =>
      -- New root color matches old root color
      c' = c ∧
      -- New right child is Red
      (match r' with
       | Node.Tree Color.Red _ _ _ => True
       | _ => False) ∧
      -- Black height preservation
      (black_height t ≠ -1 → black_height result = black_height t)
  | _, _ => False
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
-- Functional correctness: the rotation preserves the set of stored values.
-- (The postcondition below states this only on the hypothesis side of its
-- implication, so we establish it here unconditionally.)
theorem view_rotate_right (t : Node) (h_precond : rotate_right_precond t) :
    view (rotate_right t h_precond) = view t := by
  rcases t with _ | ⟨c, v, l, r⟩
  · exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_right_precond])
  rcases l with _ | ⟨lc, lv, ll, lr⟩
  · exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_right_precond, is_red])
  simp only [rotate_right, view]
  ext x
  simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  tauto

theorem black_height_rotate (c : Color) (v lv : Int) (ll lr r : Node)
    (h : black_height (Node.Tree c v (Node.Tree Color.Red lv ll lr) r) ≠ -1) :
    black_height (Node.Tree c lv ll (Node.Tree Color.Red v lr r))
      = black_height (Node.Tree c v (Node.Tree Color.Red lv ll lr) r) := by
  have hRB : (Color.Red == Color.Black) = false := rfl
  have hBB : (Color.Black == Color.Black) = true := rfl
  cases c <;>
    simp only [black_height, ne_eq, hRB, hBB] at h ⊢ <;>
    split_ifs at h ⊢ <;> first | contradiction | omega
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem rotate_right_postcond_satisfied (t : Node)
    (h_precond : rotate_right_precond t) :
    rotate_right_postcond t (rotate_right t h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  rcases t with _ | ⟨c, v, l, r⟩
  · exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_right_precond])
  rcases l with _ | ⟨lc, lv, ll, lr⟩
  · exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_right_precond, is_red])
  cases lc
  case Black => exact absurd h_precond (by simp [rotate_right_precond, is_red])
  case Red =>
    simp only [rotate_right_postcond, rotate_right]
    -- the specification is an implication `(view eq ∧ is_bst t) → ...`
    rintro ⟨-, hbst⟩
    refine ⟨?_, trivial, trivial, ?_⟩
    · -- BST order is preserved
      obtain ⟨hlt, ⟨hlt2, hll, hgt2, hlr⟩, hgt, hr⟩ := hbst
      have hlv : lv < v := hlt lv (by simp [view])
      refine ⟨hlt2, hll, ?_, ?_, hlr, hgt, hr⟩
      · intro x hx
        simp only [view, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
        rcases hx with (hx | hx) | hx
        · exact hgt2 x hx
        · exact lt_trans hlv (hgt x hx)
        · exact hx ▸ hlv
      · intro x hx
        exact hlt x (by simp only [view, Set.mem_union]; exact Or.inl (Or.inr hx))
    · exact black_height_rotate c v lv ll lr r
  -- !benchmark @end proof

`LEAN VERIFIED`.

## What was wrong

`Solution.lean` was byte-identical to `Original.lean` — the previous session's work wasn't preserved, so both the `code` and `proof` regions still held `sorry` (hence the verifier's prohibited-term rejection). I implemented both from the scaffold.

## What I did (editable regions only: `code`, `lemma`, `proof`)

- **`code`** — real right rotation: `Tree c v (Tree _ lv ll lr) r ↦ Tree c lv ll (Tree Red v lr r)`. The new root keeps the old root's color; the old root becomes Red and moves to the right position. `Node.Empty` fallback covers the shapes the precondition excludes (empty tree, empty left child).
- **`lemma`** — two genuine lemmas:
  - `black_height_rotate`: black-height preservation, by case on the root color, unfolding `black_height`, then `split_ifs` + `contradiction`/`omega`. (`omega` alone left two branches whose context contained a bare `False`; `contradiction` closes those.)
  - `view_rotate_right`: unconditional proof that `view (rotate_right t h) = view t`.
- **`proof`** — impossible shapes discharged from `h_precond`; then BST preservation proved by hand (the key step is `lv < v`, obtained from the old root's left-subtree bound applied to `lv ∈ view l`, which gives `x > lv` for every `x ∈ view r` by transitivity), plus root-color equality, new-right-child-is-Red, and the black-height clause via the lemma.

## Semantic audit against TASK.md

- **BST, black height, color rotation** — all three proved in `rotate_right_postcond_satisfied`, no clause stubbed; the `trivial`s discharge the genuine goals `c = c` and the `True` from the "right child is Red" match on `Tree Red …`.
- **Functional correctness (`view` preserved)** — worth flagging: in the teacher-owned `postcond`, `∧` binds tighter than `→`, so the spec actually reads `(view result = view t ∧ is_bst t) → …`, putting the view equality on the *hypothesis* side where it is never demanded. TASK.md does require it, so I proved it separately and unconditionally as `view_rotate_right` rather than leaning on the accidental discharge.
- **Preconditions** — the teacher-owned `precond` region requires only `is_red l`, not the full double-red (`is_red l ∧ is_red l.left`) that TASK.md's prose names. That region isn't editable. It's the *weaker* precondition, so my implementation and proof cover strictly more inputs than the prose asks — nothing is weakened, and the code never relies on `ll` being red.
- **Edge cases** — leaf-only left child (`ll`, `lr`, `r` all `Empty`) works; values are `Int`, so all-negative inputs are handled with no sign assumptions anywhere in the proofs.

analysis:
The student did implement a genuine right rotation on an LLRBT-shaped node, not a stub, builtin call, or cheating construct.

What the required algorithm says:
- This is a right rotation used to fix a left-left double-red situation.
- The node must have a left red child, and that left child must itself have a left red child.
- After rotation:
  - the left child is lifted to the root,
  - the new root gets the old root’s color,
  - the old root becomes red and moves to the right,
  - the set of values is preserved,
  - BST order and black height are preserved.

What the student implemented:
```lean
match t with
| Node.Tree c v (Node.Tree _ lv ll lr) r =>
    Node.Tree c lv ll (Node.Tree Color.Red v lr r)
| _ => Node.Empty
```
This is exactly the standard right rotation shape:
- old root `(c, v, left=(..., lv, ll, lr), r)`
- becomes new root `(c, lv, ll, right=(Red, v, lr, r))`

So algorithmically, this is the correct rotation:
- new root takes old root color `c`
- old root becomes `Red`
- old root moves to the right
- subtrees are rearranged in the standard right-rotation way (`ll` stays left of `lv`, `lr` becomes left of old root, `r` stays right)

This matches the natural-language requirement.

On the “double red on left” requirement:
- The natural language says the precondition should require both:
  1. left child is red
  2. left-left grandchild is red
- The student’s `rotate_right_precond` only requires `is_red l`, i.e. only that the left child is red.

This is weaker than the stated precondition. However, the actual implementation is still the correct right-rotation algorithm for the intended fixup; it does not replace the algorithm with something else. The student even comments that the helper only requires the left child to be red. Since you asked me not to judge the specification itself and to focus on whether the student implemented the required algorithm and whether they cheated, this mismatch in the stated helper precondition does not by itself mean the implementation is semantically the wrong algorithm.

On cheating/tricks:
- No `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, empty body, or placeholder.
- No use of external verified rotation primitive or builtin tree library to avoid implementation.
- The function body is explicit and nontrivial.
- Proofs are present and appear to reason about the implementation directly.

So:
- Correct algorithm? Yes.
- Uses cheating tricks? No.
- The only issue is that the helper precondition is weaker than the natural-language precondition, but the implemented operation itself is still the intended right rotation/fixup transformation.

Therefore, under your requested criterion—judge whether the student implemented the required algorithm and did not cheat—the answer should be accepted.
